thread:
maya: Heads-up — seeing repeated NVMe read stalls on a bunch of us-west1 GPU nodes, causing pod attach timeouts and failed gpu provisioning (timeouts ~20-30s).
sre-bot: alert: nvme_read_stall_rate high on gnode-34[us-west1] (rules/nvme_read_stalls)
oliver: I can correlate — scrub/janitor runs overlapped our nightly batch launch window yesterday.
oliver: quick snapshot of node metrics:
```
gnode-34 nvme0 read_latency_ms p95=118
read_iops  -> baseline 1100, during spike -> 60
background_scrub.running=true
```
maya: ugh. those attach timeouts bubbled into the autoscaler and we lost ~8 GPU attach attempts in the 15m window.
sam: what's changed recently? any config flips to janitor or retention?
oliver: retention for ephemeral cleanup was increased to 12h to reduce S3 churn (PR #4421) last week. that widened scrub overlap with batch windows.
deepa: increasing retention was a cost move for S3, but didn't think about local NVMe impact.
ops-lead: cost tradeoff is real — we saved ~4% monthly egress, but that's not worth widespread GPU failures.
maya: agreed. short-term mitigation ideas?
oliver: options:
  - roll retention back to 2h (fastest)
  - throttle janitor IOPS via token bucket (nice long-term)
  - move full scrubs to staggered windows (avoid batch launches)
  - add pre-attach check to prefer nodes not running scrubs (quick patch)
sre-bot: suggested runbook: if read_stall_rate > 0.05 for 10m then suspend janitor on node. (auto remediation candidate)
sam: any downsides to rolling retention back to 2h? more metadata churn, more S3 ops, small cost delta.
deepa: also wear: more frequent deletes/writes could slightly increase write amplification — need to model wear impact.
oliver: short patch I'm proposing:
  - revert retention to 2h (canary on 3 nodes in eu-west2)
  - add per-node janitor iops cap: 50MB/s
  - schedule heavy scrubs between 02:00-04:00 local region
ops-lead: can we canary eu-west2 first and then us-west1? us-west1 is busiest so safer to test elsewhere.
maya: canary OK. set rollout + automatic rollback if attach failures spike.
oliver: kubectl patch snippet for throttle (draft):
```
kubectl patch ds janitor -n infra --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"janitor.iops.max":"50MB/s"}}}}}'
```
sam: need a quick cost estimate for reverting retention (2h) vs keeping 12h and throttling. i'll ask finance for a delta.
deepa: I'll run a wear forecast for the next 3 months under 2h churn and report tomorrow.
maya: can someone open a short ticket and own the rollout? we need logs + dashboards updated.
ops-lead: assigning to @oliver for rollout plan and @sam for cost delta. @deepa does wear model. I'll monitor.
oliver: opening ticket INFRA-2839 with runbook and canary plan.
oliver: timeline: canary tonight at 23:00 UTC, monitor for 2 hours, then expand if clean.
maya: thanks — let's also update the console alert to reflect janitor-suspend state so SREs see it.
sre-bot: noted: creating alert ticket and wiring to #oncall.
ops-lead: thumbs up. if we hit regressions, rollback to 12h and enable per-node scrub staggering.
maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
sam: ping me once INFRA-2839 exists, i'll attach the cost sheet.
deepa: will post wear numbers by 12:00 UTC tomorrow.
oliver: will push canary and share logs in this thread. short term done.
maya: tracking — will be on watch during canary window.
